# Criminal Violations Criminal violations of Standard Operating Procedure are violations that exceed incompetence or carelessness and reach the threshold of violations of Space Law § 204 (Endangerment) or Space Law § 306 (Abuse of Power). Officials discovering such violations should cite as normal and inform the Security Department and the Commanding Officer at once. These include, but are not limited to:
Ethics violations -Medical procedures or research done with blatant disregard for the safety, comfort, or long term health of the subject -Experimental procedures performed without authorization by the head of staff and the consent of the subject.
Basic Rights violations -Failure to supply prisoners with food, water, and freedom of movement when there is no undue risk of harm. -Denial of access or medical treatment to a visitor when no threat or hostile intent was presented.
Safety violations -Improper storage of controlled items -Lack of protective equipment necessary in a hazardous site -Lack of available basic first aid -Creation of an unnecessary exposed health risk -Failure to establish a marked perimeter of a hazardous environment
